react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00260) as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranks this KEGG pathway first with FDR = 8.6 × 10⁻¹⁷ and 737-fold enrichment, hitting seven input metabolites (glycine, choline, adenosine, L-serine, L-cysteine, L-threonine, S-adenosylmethionine). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranks hsa00260 second (p = 3.3 × 10⁻⁷), hitting the same five amino-acid inputs. Mummichog m/z-direct activity also returns Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism as its top hit (p = 0.00244), achieving an 8-of-8 metabolite overlap — the strongest single-pathway empirical-compound enrichment in the dataset. The three-way paradigm consensus is unambiguous. Secondary pathway Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:hsa00270) is supported by RaMP (FDR = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁴, 6/51 hits) and MetaboAnalystR (p = 6 × 10⁻⁴, 3/33 hits), with S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) and L-cysteine as the bridging driver metabolites shared with the serine/threonine axis via the cystathionine γ-synthase and cystathionine β-synthase junction. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of one-carbon folate-linked amino-acid metabolism, implicating disrupted methylation capacity (SAM), altered transsulfuration flux (cysteine), and perturbed glycine cleavage. These changes are consistent with oxidative-stress or epigenetic-modulation phenotypes in the treatment condition.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converged on a single dominant biological signal: disruption of one-carbon and amino-group metabolism centred on the glycine–serine–threonine node. RaMP returned Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260) as the top hit (FDR 8.6 × 10⁻¹⁷; fold-enrichment 737; 7 of 10 input metabolites) and Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270) at rank 9 (FDR 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁴; 6 metabolites). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA ranked hsa00670 (One carbon pool by folate; p = 8.4 × 10⁻¹⁰; 6 metabolites) first and hsa00260 (Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism; p = 3.3 × 10⁻⁷; 5 metabolites) second. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently ranked Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism as the top m/z-matched pathway (p = 0.0024; 6 metabolites) and Methionine and cysteine metabolism second (p = 0.010; 5 metabolites). The tyrosine-metabolism hit in Mummichog (p = 0.047; 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde, the only input not fitting the amino-acid cluster) reflects the remaining outlier input compound. Cross-paradigm driver metabolites are glycine (C00037), L-serine (C00065), L-threonine (C00188), choline (C00114), L-cysteine (C00097), adenosine (C00212), and S-adenosylmethionine (C00019), all verified as pathway members by the enrichment methods. The convergence across ORA (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR) and m/z network (Mummichog) paradigms, spanning KEGG and WikiPathways namespaces, strongly implicates coordinated perturbation of one-carbon folate cycling and amino-group transfer as the primary biological effect in the treatment group.

  "narrative_text": "The differential metabolomics dataset of 10 metabolites was interrogated across three complementary paradigms: RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct pathway activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA. All three methods converged on a dominant signal in one-carbon amino-acid metabolism. The single strongest cross-paradigm winner is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260), which ranked 1st in RaMP ORA (FDR = 8.6e-17, fold enrichment = 737), 1st in Mummichog (p = 0.0013), and 2nd in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 3.3e-07). Six input metabolites—glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-serine (KEGG:C00065), choline (KEGG:C00114), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), and S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019)—were confirmed as hits by RaMP within this pathway. The second major winner, Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270 / hsa00270), ranked 9th in RaMP (FDR = 1.1e-14), 1st in Mummichog for methionine/cysteine metabolism (p = 0.007), and 3rd in MetaboAnalystR (p = 6e-04), with S-adenosylmethionine, L-serine, and L-cysteine as shared hits. A third hub, One carbon pool by folate (KEGG:hsa00670), was the top MetaboAnalystR hit (p = 8.4e-10) and overlapped six input metabolites via the same one-carbon donor/acceptor logic. S-adenosylmethionine is the central methyl-group donor linking glycine–serine flux to methionine cycling, while adenosine (KEGG:C00212) participates as the adenine moiety recycled during S-adenosylmethionine synthesis. Choline oxidation intermediates (via glycine betaine) bridge the methionine cycle to the folate-dependent one-carbon pool. Sucrose (KEGG:C00089) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C04043) represent peripheral hits: the former maps to disaccharide metabolism and sialic acid biosynthesis in Mummichog; the latter is a specific probe of tyrosine catabolism. The consistent driver pattern (glycine, serine, methionine, cysteine, choline, adenosine) points to an integrated perturbation of methyl-group metabolism and connected sulfur amino-acid handling. Cross-paradigm concordance was high between RaMP and Mummichog; MetaboAnalystR KEGG-namespace results aligned on the same metabolic modules with slightly different ranking due to library scope. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolomics dataset of 10 metabolites was interrogated across three complementary paradigms: RaMP multi-database ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct pathway activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA. All three methods converged on a dominant signal in one-carbon amino-acid metabolism. The single strongest cross-paradigm winner is Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG:map00260 / hsa00260), which ranked 1st in RaMP ORA (FDR = 8.6e-17, fold enrichment = 737), 1st in Mummichog (p = 0.0013), and 2nd in MetaboAnalystR PSEA (p = 3.3e-07). Six input metabolites—glycine (KEGG:C00037), L-serine (KEGG:C00065), choline (KEGG:C00114), L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), and S-adenosylmethionine (KEGG:C00019)—were confirmed as hits by RaMP within this pathway. The second major winner, Methionine Metabolism (KEGG:map00270 / hsa00270), ranked 9th in RaMP (FDR = 1.1e-14), 1st in Mummichog for methionine/cysteine metabolism (p = 0.007), and 3rd in MetaboAnalystR (p = 6e-04), with S-adenosylmethionine, L-serine, and L-cysteine as shared hits. A third hub, One carbon pool by folate (KEGG:hsa00670), was the top MetaboAnalystR hit (p = 8.4e-10) and overlapped six input metabolites via the same one-carbon donor/acceptor logic. S-adenosylmethionine is the central methyl-group donor linking glycine–serine flux to methionine cycling, while adenosine (KEGG:C00212) participates as the adenine moiety recycled during S-adenosylmethionine synthesis. Choline oxidation intermediates (via glycine betaine) bridge the methionine cycle to the folate-dependent one-carbon pool. Sucrose (KEGG:C00089) and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde (KEGG:C04043) represent peripheral hits: the former maps to disaccharide metabolism and sialic acid biosynthesis in Mummichog; the latter is a specific probe of tyrosine catabolism. The consistent driver pattern (glycine, serine, methionine, cysteine, choline, adenosine) points to an integrated perturbation of methyl-group metabolism and connected sulfur amino-acid handling. Cross-paradigm concordance was high between RaMP and Mummichog; MetaboAnalystR KEGG-namespace results aligned on the same metabolic modules with slightly different ranking due to library scope. Limitations: FELLA graph-diffusion was unavailable at the time of analysis; L-2-amino-3-oxobutanoic acid (KEGG:C03508) did not map strongly in any single pathway but may represent a downstream cataplerotic signature of amino-acid cataplerosis.
